key_insight: For bounded-degree max-Ek-LINSAT over finite fields, the best possible improvement over random guessing scales only as O(1/√D), and decoded quantum interferometry can match this limit only with quantum decoding.
engineering_relevance: This sets a hard benchmark for quantum and classical solvers on sparse constraint instances, showing that any advantage is limited to constants and depends critically on the decoder design.
method: Extended NP-hardness results from Boolean bounded-degree Max-LINSAT to max-Ek-LINSAT(q,r) over arbitrary finite fields.
Proved hardness to beat the random baseline r/q by more than Oq,r(1/√D) for bounded degree D.
Analyzed decoded quantum interferometry on (k,D)-regular instances and compared classical vs quantum decoders.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a complexity-theoretic hardness bound, not an empirical benchmark: exceeding r/q by more than Oq,r(1/√D) is NP-hard, and classical DQI is further limited to 1/√(D log D).
watch_item: The result is asymptotic and worst-case; practical performance may still depend strongly on instance structure, decoder choice, and hidden constant factors.
paper_title: Approximability limits for bounded-degree max-LINSAT and implications for decoded quantum interferometry
